#!/bin/bash

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables in an unquoted
# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=pods
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, res: [.spec.containers[] | {n: .name, req: .resources.requests, lim: .resources.limits}], qos: .status.qosClass}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)
# `kubectl api-resources` sorts by group name, so a CRD reusing a built-in
# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -c .)" -gt 1 ] && [[ "$API_INFO" != *" v1 "* ]]; then
  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)

  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else

    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination

CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then

#!/bin/bash

# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables in an unquoted
# assignment slot, then reference them only as "$VAR". Never interpolate
#  inside a quoted context - sanitize() (shlex.quote) wraps
# dangerous values in single quotes, which are literal (and command
# substitution stays active) inside a double-quoted or single-quoted slot.
KIND=networkchaos
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""

# Collapse multi-line jq expressions (LLMs sometimes write multi-line jq)
# Note: use $'\n' syntax instead of '\n' because Jinja2 interprets \n as literal newlines
JQ_FILTER='.items[] | {name: .metadata.name, kind: .kind}'
JQ_FILTER=$(printf '%s' "$JQ_FILTER" | tr $'\n\r' '  ')

err_file=$(mktemp)
PROCESSED=0
NOTES='[]'
SCOPE='null'

add_note() {
  NOTES=$(jq -c --arg note "$1" '. + [$note]' <<< "$NOTES")
}

uri_encode() {
  jq -rn --arg v "$1" '$v|@uri'
}

fail() {
  err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
  rm -f "$err_file"
  jq -n --arg stderr "$1 $err_content" --argjson total "$PROCESSED" --argjson notes "$NOTES" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    '{total_items_processed: $total, matches_found: 0, results: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  exit 0
}

# The namespace becomes part of the raw API path, so anything other than a valid
# namespace name (e.g. 'default/services/x:80/proxy/?') could reach other API endpoints
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && ! [[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" =~ ^[a-z0-9]([-a-z0-9]{0,61}[a-z0-9])?$ ]]; then
  fail "Invalid namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}': must be a Kubernetes namespace name (lowercase letters, digits and '-')."
fi

# Get the API path for the resource kind using kubectl
# Match the resource name (first column) as an EXACT string, not a
# grep regex - otherwise a kind like '.*' or 'a|b' would match the
# wrong resource.
CANDIDATES=$(kubectl api-resources --no-headers 2>>"$err_file" | awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind')
API_INFO=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | head -1)
# `kubectl api-resources` sorts by group name, so a CRD reusing a built-in
# plural (e.g. Calico's crd.projectcalico.org networkpolicies) can be listed
# before networking.k8s.io. Pick what `kubectl get` picks: the core group,
# then the first group in server discovery order (/apis).
if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -c .)" -gt 1 ] && [[ "$API_INFO" != *" v1 "* ]]; then
  API_GROUPS=$(kubectl get --raw /apis 2>/dev/null | jq -r '.groups[].name' 2>/dev/null)
  if [ -z "$API_GROUPS" ]; then
    add_note "Several API groups serve '${KIND}' and server discovery (/apis) failed, so the first group listed by kubectl api-resources was used."
  fi
  for group in $API_GROUPS; do
    match=$(printf '%s\n' "$CANDIDATES" | grep -F " $group/" | head -1)
    if [ -n "$match" ]; then
      API_INFO="$match"
      break
    fi
  done
fi

if [ -z "$API_INFO" ]; then
  fail "Unable to find resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Extract NAMESPACED value
if [[ "$API_INFO" == *" true "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=true
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ true .*//')
elif [[ "$API_INFO" == *" false "* ]]; then
  NAMESPACED=false
  PREFIX=$(echo "$API_INFO" | sed 's/ false .*//')
else
  fail "Could not parse API info for '${KIND}'."
fi

# Trim trailing spaces from prefix and collapse internal spaces
PREFIX=$(echo "$PREFIX" | sed 's/  *$//' | sed 's/  */ /g')

IFS=' ' read -ra PREFIX_FIELDS <<< "$PREFIX"
FIELD_COUNT=0
for field in "${PREFIX_FIELDS[@]}"; do
  ((FIELD_COUNT++))
done

RESOURCE_NAME="${PREFIX_FIELDS[0]}"
if [ $FIELD_COUNT -ge 2 ]; then
  API_VERSION="${PREFIX_FIELDS[$((FIELD_COUNT - 1))]}"
else
  API_VERSION=""
fi

if [ -z "$API_VERSION" ] || [ -z "$RESOURCE_NAME" ]; then
  fail "Unable to parse API info for resource kind '${KIND}'."
fi

# Build API path: namespaced kinds can be listed within one namespace;
# cluster-scoped kinds ignore the namespace (as kubectl does)
if [[ "$API_VERSION" == "v1" ]]; then
  API_BASE="/api/v1"
else
  API_BASE="/apis/${API_VERSION}"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

#!/bin/bash
# SECURITY: assign sanitized params to shell variables (unquoted slot),
# then reference them only as "$VAR" - never interpolate 
# inside a quoted context. See kubernetes_jq_query for the rationale.
KIND=resourcequotas
CUSTOM_COLUMNS=NAME:.metadata.name,KIND:.kind
# 'namespace' is also a Jinja global (namespace()), so it is defined even when omitted
SEL_NAMESPACE=boutique
SEL_LABELS=
SEL_FIELDS=
FILTER_PATTERN=
# Strict tool calls send null for unset optional params, which renders as 'None'
[ "$SEL_NAMESPACE" = "None" ] && SEL_NAMESPACE=""
[ "$SEL_LABELS" = "None" ] && SEL_LABELS=""
[ "$SEL_FIELDS" = "None" ] && SEL_FIELDS=""
[ "$FILTER_PATTERN" = "None" ] && FILTER_PATTERN=""

# kubectl ignores -n for cluster-scoped kinds; say so instead of reporting a namespace that wasn't applied
NOTES='[]'
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
  is_kind() { awk -v kind="$KIND" '$1 == kind || index($1, kind ".") == 1 {found = 1} END {exit !found}'; }
  if kubectl api-resources --namespaced=false -o name 2>/dev/null | is_kind \
    && ! kubectl api-resources --namespaced=true -o name 2>/dev/null | is_kind; then
    NOTES=$(jq -nc --arg note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${KIND} is cluster-scoped." '[$note]')
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
fi

SCOPE_ARGS=()
if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-n "$SEL_NAMESPACE")
else
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--all-namespaces)
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(-l "$SEL_LABELS")
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SCOPE_ARGS+=(--field-selector "$SEL_FIELDS")
fi

err_file=$(mktemp)
output=$(kubectl get "$KIND" "${SCOPE_ARGS[@]}" -o custom-columns="$CUSTOM_COLUMNS" 2>"$err_file")
kubectl_exit=$?
err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

SCOPE='null'
if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
    '{namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
      label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
      field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')
fi

if [ $kubectl_exit -ne 0 ] || [ -z "$output" ]; then
  if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
    jq -n --arg stderr "$err_content" --argjson scope "$SCOPE" --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
      '{count: 0, header: null, rows: [], stderr: $stderr, scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
  else
    echo "=== STDERR ==="
    echo "$err_content"
    echo "=== ROWS ==="
    echo "=== COUNT ==="
    echo 0
  fi
  exit 0
fi

# Split header and data rows
header=$(echo "$output" | head -1)
if [ -n "$FILTER_PATTERN" ]; then
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2 | grep -E -- "$FILTER_PATTERN" || true)
else
  data=$(echo "$output" | tail -n +2)
fi

if command -v jq &>/dev/null; then
  if [ -n "$data" ]; then
    count=$(echo "$data" | wc -l)
  else
    count=0
  fi
  # Rows go through stdin, not --argjson, so large tables don't hit "Argument list too long"
  printf '%s' "$data" | jq -R . | jq -s \
    --argjson count "$count" \
    --arg header "$header" \
    --arg stderr "$err_content" \
    --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
    --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
    '{count: $count, header: $header, rows: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'
else
  echo "=== STDERR ==="
  echo "$err_content"
  echo "=== HEADER ==="
  echo "$header"
  echo "=== ROWS ==="

if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ] && [ "$NAMESPACED" = "true" ]; then
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/namespaces/${SEL_NAMESPACE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
else
  if [ -n "$SEL_NAMESPACE" ]; then
    add_note "namespace '${SEL_NAMESPACE}' ignored: ${RESOURCE_NAME} is cluster-scoped."
    SEL_NAMESPACE=""
  fi
  API_PATH="${API_BASE}/${RESOURCE_NAME}"
fi

SELECTOR_QUERY=""
if [ -n "$SEL_LABELS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&labelSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_LABELS")"
fi
if [ -n "$SEL_FIELDS" ]; then
  SELECTOR_QUERY="${SELECTOR_QUERY}&fieldSelector=$(uri_encode "$SEL_FIELDS")"
fi

SCOPE=$(jq -nc --arg resource "$RESOURCE_NAME" --arg api_version "$API_VERSION" \
  --arg namespace "$SEL_NAMESPACE" --arg labels "$SEL_LABELS" --arg fields "$SEL_FIELDS" \
  '{resource: $resource, api_version: $api_version,
    namespace: (if $namespace == "" then null else $namespace end),
    label_selector: (if $labels == "" then null else $labels end),
    field_selector: (if $fields == "" then null else $fields end)}')

# Process resources in chunks using API pagination
LIMIT=500
CONTINUE=""
TOTAL_MATCHES=0
ALL_MATCHES=""

while true; do
  QUERY="${API_PATH}?limit=${LIMIT}${SELECTOR_QUERY}"
  if [ -n "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    # continue tokens are base64 and may contain '+', '/' or '='
    QUERY="${QUERY}&continue=$(uri_encode "$CONTINUE")"
  fi

  OUTPUT=$(kubectl get --raw "$QUERY" 2>>"$err_file")
  exit_code=$?

  if [ $exit_code -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "kubectl get --raw failed for $QUERY."
  fi

  ITEMS_COUNT=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq '.items | length')

  MATCHES=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -c "$JQ_FILTER" 2>>"$err_file")
  jq_exit=$?
  if [ $jq_exit -ne 0 ]; then
    fail "jq expression failed."
  fi

  if [ "$ITEMS_COUNT" -gt 0 ]; then
    if [ -n "$MATCHES" ]; then
      if [ -z "$ALL_MATCHES" ]; then
        ALL_MATCHES="$MATCHES"
      else
        ALL_MATCHES="$ALL_MATCHES"$'\n'"$MATCHES"
      fi
      MATCH_COUNT=$(echo "$MATCHES" | grep -c . || true)
      TOTAL_MATCHES=$((TOTAL_MATCHES + MATCH_COUNT))
    fi
    PROCESSED=$((PROCESSED + ITEMS_COUNT))
  fi

  CONTINUE=$(echo "$OUTPUT" | jq -r '.metadata.continue // empty')

  if [ -z "$CONTINUE" ]; then
    break
  fi
done

err_content=$(cat "$err_file" 2>/dev/null)
rm -f "$err_file"

# Output results as a JSON object with metadata. Results go through stdin, not --argjson:
# Linux caps a single argument at 128KB, so larger results failed with "Argument list too long".
printf '%s\n' "$ALL_MATCHES" | jq -s \
  --argjson total_items_processed "$PROCESSED" \
  --argjson matches_found "$TOTAL_MATCHES" \
  --arg stderr "$err_content" \
  --argjson scope "$SCOPE" \
  --argjson notes "$NOTES" \
  '{total_items_processed: $total_items_processed, matches_found: $matches_found, results: ., stderr: (if $stderr == "" then null else $stderr end), scope: $scope, notes: $notes}'

## 结论：瓶颈在「购物车存储」这条链路（frontend → cartservice → redis-cart），不在应用逻辑

所有页面现在都在 **286–345 ms** 返回 200，而出故障前的基线是 **7–26 ms**（12:41–12:48 的 frontend 日志）。同一时期后端各服务自身处理都是亚毫秒级，说明慢在**每个页面都要调用的那一段**：每个页面（`/`、`/product/*`、`/cart`、`/cart/checkout`）都会调用 `getCart`，而 `cartservice → redis-cart` 这一段自 12:49:40 起变得不稳定。

### 时间线（均已确认）

| 时间 (UTC) | 事实 |
|---|---|
| 12:41–12:48 | 正常：`GET /` 15–36 ms，`/product/*` 7–12 ms，`/cart` 8–9 ms，`POST /cart/checkout` 13 ms，`POST /cart` 2 ms |
| **12:49:40–12:50:30** | 页面全部 500，耗时 5.1–5.8 s。cartservice 日志（12:48–12:52 共 690 行异常）反复输出：`Can't access cart storage. RedisConnectionException: The message timed out in the backlog attempting to send because no connection became available (5000ms) — Last Connection Exception: SocketClosed (ReadEndOfStream, last-recv: 0) on redis-cart:6379 ... ws: Initializing, async-ops: 2329`；frontend 对应错误为 `could not retrieve cart` / `failed to add to cart` / `failed to complete the order ... cart failure: failed to get user cart during checkout` |
| 12:50:30–13:10:27 | 错误消失，但进入高延迟状态：`/product/*` **2071–2202 ms**、`/cart` **1762–2796 ms**、`POST /cart/checkout` 2362–2801 ms；loadgenerator 记录最高 **19.5 s** |
| 13:00:07 | productcatalogservice 被 **手动重启**（pod 注解 `kubectl.kubernetes.io/restartedAt: 2026-11-15T13:00:07Z`，deployment revision 4） |
| 13:01:49–13:03 | recommendationservice 出现约 55 次 gRPC `UNAVAILABLE / grpc_status:14`、`Connection refused → 10.96.32.253:3550`（productcatalogservice 的 ClusterIP，重启期间 endpoint 为空） |
| 13:03:27 / 13:03:36 | checkoutservice pod 被重建；redis-cart 被 **手动重启**（`restartedAt: 13:03:36Z`，revision 4）；checkoutservice revision 7。其余 9 个 deployment 都是 revision 1 |
| 13:10:27 起至今 | 页面降到 **286–345 ms**（仍为基线 8–12 ms 的 25–40 倍），无任何 5xx、无重启 |

### 关键量化证据（排除应用代码与资源配额）

- 后端处理本身极快：shippingservice `GetQuote`/`ShipOrder` 收到→完成 **0.05 ms**；paymentservice 服务端日志与 checkoutservice 收到响应同一毫秒（**0–1 ms**）；currencyservice 一次页面请求的 10 次 `conversion` 在 **5 ms** 内完成；redis `BGSAVE` 100 ms 完成、`100 changes in 300 seconds`（进程不忙）。
- 但跨 pod 调用很慢：cart 页面 337 ms 中有 **332 ms 花在 shipping quote 之前的 getCurrencies+getCart+getRecommendations**，quote 之后只剩 4.5 ms；checkout 流程 PlaceOrder→扣款 **294 ms**，而其内部 payment RPC 只是 0–1 ms。
- 目前最慢的单点：`POST /cart`（addToCart = getProduct + 写购物车）**585–612 ms**，而完全不碰后端的 `POST /setCurrency` 是 **0 ms**；即写购物车约 575 ms、读约 250–300 ms。
- 资源/配置无异常：12 个 pod 全部 Running/Ready、**restartCount 0**、endpoint 全就绪；镜像与 resources 与官方 microservices-demo v0.10.3 清单一致（frontend/productcatalog 200m、redis-cart 125m 等），无 ResourceQuota/LimitRange，探针每 10 s 命中且 `took_ms:0`（node→pod 通路与调度正常）。
- **代码/config 没被改坏**：13:00/13:03 的三次重启都是 `rollout restart`（restartedAt 注解、revision 由 1 变 4/7），`last-applied-configuration` 与当前 spec 完全一致——这些重启是有人在救火，且没有改变任何配置（也几乎没改善延迟）。

### 影响面

- **受影响**：frontend（当前 286–345 ms/页，12:49:45–12:50:28 有 5xx；12:50–13:10 为 2.1–2.8 s）、cartservice（`RedisConnectionException` ×690、`FailedPrecondition` 返回）、redis-cart（对端 `SocketClosed/ReadEndOfStream`，13:03:36 被重启）、recommendationservice（13:01–13:03 对 productcatalog 的 `grpc_status:14`）、loadgenerator（618 次失败请求、最高 19.5 s）。
- **已检查、健康**：adservice、currencyservice、emailservice、paymentservice、shippingservice、productcatalogservice、checkoutservice（均无错误，处理亚毫秒）。
- **未检查/无权限**：节点状态与节点 CPU/内存（`nodes is forbidden`）、其他命名空间、容器 CPU 限流指标（live-metrics/Prometheus 未配置）、网络抓包（`cilium`/`hubble` 二进制不存在、`ENABLE_INSPEKTOR_GADGET` 未设置）。

### 根因候选（按可能性排序）与验证方法

1. **redis-cart 的连接通路不稳定**（最可能）：证据是 `SocketClosed (ReadEndOfStream)` 形式的对端连接被断、`no connection became available (5000ms)`、`ws: Initializing`，而 redis 进程自身日志干净、命令极少。这更像节点上 conntrack/kube-proxy/CNI 层面丢包或连接重置，而不是 redis 自身负载。→ 需 `cilium status`/`hubble observe`（当前工具不可用）、节点 `dmesg`/`conntrack -S`、`kubectl describe node` 检查是否 Pressure。
2. **cartservice 的 StackExchange.Redis 客户端处于劣化状态**：该 pod 自 12:30:32 起从未重启，而它依赖的 redis 在 12:49 断连、13:03 被整体替换；日志里 `async-ops: 2329`、`qu: 5` 的发送积压正是“连接不可用后回填”的典型症状。**最值得立刻尝试的修复：`kubectl -n boutique rollout restart deployment/cartservice`**，观察 286–345 ms 与 `POST /cart` 585 ms 是否回到 8–12 ms。
3. **redis-cart CPU limit 过低（125m，命名空间内最紧）+ 单节点 CPU 争用**：可放大每次命令的等待，表现为读 ~250 ms / 写 ~575 ms 的抖动。→ 用 `kubectl top pod -n boutique`、`kubectl top node`、`container_cpu_cfs_throttled_periods` 验证，必要时把 redis-cart limit 提到 300–500m。
4. 次要/并行问题（已自愈，但会造成“看不到错误”的短暂降级）：productcatalogservice 重启期间 endpoint 为空导致 recommendationservice 报错，以及 12:49–12:50 的 5xx 窗口；这些都不解释当前仍在的 ~300 ms。

建议顺序：先重启 cartservice（改动最小、直击客户端积压）→ 不行则查节点网络/CPU（需要 nodes、cilium/hubble、metrics 权限）→ 最后放宽 redis-cart 的 CPU limit。

messages.reasoning_content:
Confirmed: 10.96.32.253 = productcatalogservice ClusterIP. Connection refused at 13:01:49 → productcatalogservice had no ready endpoints at that time, despite the pod starting 13:00:07. Hmm — the pod became Ready at 13:00:09. Unless the connection refused happened because the pods were being replaced again? Actually the recommendation pod logs I saw had "created_time:2026-11-15T13:01:49" — that's from grpc channel. So at 13:01:49 the service had no endpoints. But productcatalog pod was Ready from 13:00:09 with same IP? Actually the pod could have been recreated again at 13:01:xx and the pod I see was from 13:00:07 — no, pod creation is 13:00:07 and running since 13:00:08 continuously.

Hmm, unless there were TWO pods and the other... Only 1 pod.

Alternatively, kube-proxy/iptables rules not yet updated? Or connection refused due to the pod's port not accepting connections early. Whatever — 13:01:49 is a blip, minor.

Now the crucial question: what causes the sustained latency? Let me get endpoints and check whether each service has endpoints. Also, currencyservice served 13,546 log lines in 15 min, so it's busy.

Let me now think about what could inject ~2s latency. Notice: cart page ~2.4s, product page ~2.1s. Both include productcatalog.GetProduct + currency conversions. The home page "/" was 337ms (recent). Home page = ListProducts + currency (getCurrencies/conversion) + ads? Actually home calls: getCurrencies, getProducts(ListProducts), convertCurrency for each product, GetAds. Product page: GetProduct, getCurrencies, convertCurrency x2, ListRecommendations, GetAds.

So the product page at 2.1s vs home at 337ms. Difference: ListRecommendations (recommendationservice) — which calls productcatalog ListProducts and is Python and has CPU limit 200m with 220Mi request. So recommendationservice could be adding ~1.8s. And cart page also calls ListRecommendations (for recommendations section) — yes, cart page also has recommendations. And /cart/checkout 2.4s — checkout flow (frontend /cart/checkout calls checkoutservice; but before that the frontend shows checkout page which... no recommendations). Hmm.

Wait, but the recent requests (13:10:36-13:11) show ~300ms for product and cart pages. So slowness is intermittent/bursty, not constant. That matches 15% failures with max 14.5s.

Hmm, locust median 12ms though? Odd — that suggests many very fast requests. Maybe locust's "Med" is actually wrong column ordering... locust shows "Avg Min Max Med". Values 841, 5, 14573, 12 → 5 min, 14573 max, 12 med. Hmm avg 841 with med 12 means long tail.

Hmm wait, that's strange given frontend logs show nearly everything 300ms or 2100ms. Unless locust hits frontend-external via LoadBalancer IP... Let me re-read the frontend logs: the "request complete" logs for product pages at 13:10:36-46 were 283-337ms; at 13:08-13:10:27 were ~2100ms. So the latency jumped from 2.1s to 0.3s at about 13:10:30. That's suspicious — maybe the culprit restarted/recovered right then? Or maybe the timeouts changed.

Actually! Maybe the slowdown period correlates with something. Let me get a longer view: count slow requests over time. I can't aggregate directly, but I can fetch logs in specific windows and see the pattern.

Alternative plan: use bash tool. Is bash available? "bash: Execute bash commands validated against prefix-based allow/deny lists" — listed among disabled toolsets? It says disabled toolsets... bash is listed in the "Disabled" list implicitly (all not marked FAILED are unconfigured). So no bash.

OK, let's reason with logs. Key: which service is the bottleneck. Let's check the loadgenerator's earlier stats to see the trend over time (locust prints stats periodically). If we fetch oldest logs we can see the trend. Let's fetch loadgenerator logs with a filter on "Aggregated" to see trend over the whole time.

Also check recommendationservice logs for latency, and check whether it logs the product catalog call duration.

Let me fetch loadgenerator Aggregated lines over the past hour — that gives the timeline of avg latency. Filter 'Aggregated'.

Also check endpoints objects to see if all services have ready endpoints.

Also, importantly: check if there is a LimitRange, ResourceQuota — quota exhaustion wouldn't cause slowness.

Another important thing to check: are there any pods in the boutique namespace with init containers or unusual? No.

Let's also consider: same node for all pods (control-plane). Single-node lab. Node CPU oversubscribed → CFS throttling → latency spikes. That's a plausible root cause: many pods on one node with tight CPU limits; the node may be saturated. But we can't query nodes (forbidden) and metrics are disabled.

Hmm, but there might be something else: check kube-system? Probably forbidden.

Let's try namespace-scoped listing for a few namespaces to see if chaos tooling exists (chaos-mesh, litmus).

Actually, a much better diagnostic: cgroup CPU throttling is visible inside pods at /sys/fs/cgroup... can't exec.

Let's check the recommended approach: look at pod logs for evidence. adservice is Java: it logs "received ad request" etc. Java with 300m limit and 200m request; JVM startup. Java GC could be slow. adservice logs 2493 lines in 10 min.

Let me fetch adservice logs properly (filter 'null' string was the issue — pass filter as empty?). The tool seems to treat "null" string as a filter. Earlier for loadgenerator I passed filter null and got results... inconsistent. Let me pass filter="" maybe. I'll use filter ".*" perhaps.

Plan of calls:
1. loadgenerator logs filtered 'Aggregated' with limit 200, start -3600 → trend.
2. adservice logs with filter '.*' limit 40.
3. endpoints query.
4. Try pods in chaos-mesh namespace.

SMOKING GUN FOUND:

At 12:49:45–12:50:28, the frontend returned 500s because **cartservice could not reach redis-cart**: 

`StackExchange.Redis.RedisConnectionException: The message timed out in the backlog attempting to send because no connection became available (5000ms) - Last Connection Exception: SocketClosed (ReadEndOfStream, last-recv: 0) on redis-cart:6379/Interactive, ... state: ConnectedEstablished, ... command=HMGET, timeout: 5000`

Note "SocketClosed (ReadEndOfStream, last-recv: 0)" — the socket was closed by the peer / connection dropped. Initially at 12:49:45-12:50:28 the frontend returned 500 with 5.3-5.8s.

So redis-cart became unreachable at ~12:49:40. That's the onset! And redis-cart was later restarted at 13:03:36 (restartedAt annotation) — an operator intervention. And productcatalogservice restarted at 13:00:07, checkoutservice 13:03:27.

But NOW: cart operations work (carts show items, pages 200) but slow. And the current cart-page latency: getCurrencies+getCart+getRecommendations ~332ms.

Hmm! So what is the CURRENT root cause? Now cart works. But pages are 300ms.

Wait — maybe the redis slowness is still there but less fatal: redis commands taking ~150ms each (no longer timing out at 5s). The cart service's Redis timeout is 5000ms; slow responses (150ms) don't error.

Hmm, but the checkout→payment hop was 0ms and other hops ~150ms. The pattern of "each hop ~150ms" remains unexplained by redis alone... unless:

Actually let's reconsider! What if the ~150-300ms delays are all caused by *cartservice↔redis* and the pages I measured mostly involve the cart? Let's check:
- cart page: getCart (→redis) = slow ✓ (332ms before quote ≈ currency+cart+recommendations)
- product page: does it call getCart? In v0.10.3, productHandler does NOT call getCart... but the *base template* renders cart size? Hmm, actually in the demo, the header shows the cart item count — let me recall: frontend's home.go/product.go handlers... The layout template shows "cart" badge? I believe the base template does not fetch the cart; the cart page does.

But product pages take 300ms too, and home 300ms.

Hmm, so what's common to home, product, and cart? getCurrencies. And ads. 

Hmm! Home page: getCurrencies, getProducts, converts, getAds = 300ms.
Product page: getProduct, getCurrencies, getRecommendations, converts, getAds = 300ms.
Cart page: getCurrencies, getCart, getRecommendations, shipping, products, converts = 337ms.

All ~300ms. Hmm, if each page has ~5-6 RPCs at ~50-60ms each → 300ms. So each RPC ~50-60ms, uniformly.

And redis timeouts at 12:49 show 5s connection issues. So the network was broken then.

The most parsimonious: the pod-to-pod network is degraded (each round trip ~50-150ms, occasional 5s+ timeouts leading to errors, packet loss/read-end-of-stream socket closes). This is consistent with the redis SocketClosed/ReadEndOfStream errors: connections being reset.

So: the root cause is a network-level failure between pods on this node (packet loss / connection resets), which at 12:49-12:50 caused total failures, and now manifests as ~50-150ms added per RPC (delays from retransmits), no errors.

Now — why did it start at ~12:49:40 and why did redis specifically time out then? Possibly the CNI/kube-proxy/conntrack broke. Or someone injected network chaos at ~12:49. Or node network interface issues.

If packets were dropped, we'd see timeouts rather than read-end-of-stream (RST/FIN). ReadEndOfStream = the peer closed the connection gracefully/abruptly — e.g. redis restarting, or the node's conntrack dropping.

Hmm! So maybe redis-cart went down/OOM at 12:49:40 and stayed broken (CrashLoop) until the operator restarted the deployment at 13:03:36. Then afterwards, cart works but slowly...?

But now cart pages return 200 with items — so redis works.

But then why is the app still 300ms slow today? Maybe because redis is at 200Mi request / 256Mi limit and is swapping/being throttled? Or maybe a *different* cause for the residual slowness (which existed even at 13:10:27+).
